harmonic.title: Harmonic mixing
harmonic.lead: Two tracks in compatible keys sound good together: during the transition their melodies and basslines don't clash. Tonalia detects the key of every track and tells you which ones fit.

sections.heading: The harmonic wheel
body: The wheel arranges the 24 keys in a circle of fifths: each step around it changes a single note of the scale. The outer ring holds the major keys (B) and the inner ring the minor keys (A). Every number has its own colour, so compatible tracks also look alike.
A major key shares all its notes with the minor key of the same number: {{k8B}} and {{k8A}} are relatives.

sections.heading: Safe moves
body: Same key ({{k8A}} → {{k8A}}): the smoothest possible transition.
±1 on the wheel ({{k8A}} → {{k7A}} or {{k9A}}): one note changes; it sounds natural and keeps the mood.
Relative ({{k8A}} → {{k8B}}): the same notes with a different character. Minor to major brightens the music; the other way darkens it.
Diagonal ({{k8A}} → {{k9B}}): one step plus a change of mode. It works best with a short transition or over a part without melody.
+2 energy boost ({{k8A}} → {{k10A}}): two steps on the wheel give an energy lift. Use it now and then, not in every mix.
Half step up ({{k8A}} → {{k3A}}): the key rises one semitone, a classic way to lift the floor at the right moment.

sections.heading: Using it in Tonalia
body: In a track's detail, click any key on the wheel to see the tracks in your library that are compatible with it. In Filters you can pick several keys and turn on “Include compatible”.
When the analysis is not confident, the key chip has a dashed border: check it by ear with the piano in the detail view.

sections.heading: Trust your ears
body: Theory helps you choose, but it doesn't replace listening. A track with little melody (just drums and bass) mixes with almost any key, and two compatible tracks can still clash if their melodies play together for a long time.

energy.title: Energy levels
energy.lead: Energy, from 1 to 10, sums up how intense a track feels: perceived loudness, density of hits, percussion, low end and brightness. It helps you plan the journey of a set.

sections.heading: What each level means
body: 1–3: ambient, intros and chill-out.
4–5: warm-up and laid-back grooves.
6–7: a full floor; the main body of the night.
8–10: peak moments, the most intense tracks.

sections.heading: How it is measured
body: Tonalia splits the track into 8-bar blocks and measures each one. The track's energy is the average of its more intense half, so a quiet intro doesn't lower the score of a powerful track. The per-block curve is drawn over the waveform in the detail view.

sections.heading: Building a set
body: Climb gradually: steps of one or two levels keep the floor with you, while a jump of four usually feels abrupt.
Alternate rises with small dips so the peak stands out, and at the end bring the energy down calmly instead of cutting it off.

sections.heading: Make it fit your music
body: Energy is relative to your library and your genre. If a value doesn't convince you, change it in “Edit info”: your edits take precedence over the analysis.

cues.title: Cue points and phrasing
cues.lead: Dance music is built in phrases of 8, 16 and 32 bars. Cue points mark where each section starts so you can jump to it and start your mixes in the right place.

sections.heading: Bars and phrases
body: A bar has 4 beats. The big changes (the bass comes in, the drop hits, the breakdown starts) almost always land at the start of an 8, 16 or 32-bar phrase.
If you start the mix at the beginning of a phrase, the changes in both tracks line up and the transition sounds deliberate.

sections.heading: Automatic cues
body: Tonalia places up to 8 cues per track, always on the first beat of a bar: cue 1 on the first downbeat and the rest on the most important section changes (drop, breakdown, second drop and outro). Each kind of section has its own colour.

sections.heading: Editing and setting cues
body: In the detail view you can drag a cue on the waveform, rename it, change its colour or delete it. “Set cue here” stores the playback position snapped to the nearest beat.
Cues you edit are never overwritten when you reanalyse; “Reset automatic” brings back the ones from the analysis.

sections.heading: Jumping between cues
body: Press 1 to 8 to jump to a cue and the space bar to play or pause. When you export to your DJ software, cues travel with their name and colour.

stems.title: Mashups with stems
stems.lead: A mashup plays parts of two tracks at once, for example the vocals of one over the instrumental of another. Splitting a track into stems (vocals, drums, bass and the rest) is what makes it possible.

sections.heading: What to combine
body: The safest combination is vocals over an instrumental: the two parts don't fight for the same space. Look for compatible keys and close tempos.

sections.heading: Key and tempo
body: Shifting one or two semitones up or down can make a pair compatible that wasn't. Beyond two semitones the voice usually changes timbre noticeably, and with big tempo differences the change in speed is audible too.

sections.heading: Phrasing
body: Line both tracks up at the start of a phrase: the vocals should come in where the instrumental changes, not in the middle of a phrase.

sections.heading: In Tonalia
body: Pro mode, still in development, will split stems on your computer, suggest pairs with the reason behind each idea and let you try them in sync.

errors.engineNotRunning: The analysis engine is not running yet. Tonalia is starting it: try again in a few seconds.
errors.engineExited: The analysis engine closed while working. It restarts on its own: try again.
errors.engineTimeout: The analysis engine is taking too long to answer. Try again; if it keeps happening, restart Tonalia.
errors.engineIo: Tonalia could not talk to the analysis engine. It restarts on its own: try again.
errors.offline: No internet connection, or the server is not answering.
errors.noRelease: No version has been published yet.
errors.updateSignature: The update does not have a valid signature and was not installed.
errors.licensesMissing: The licence list is not available in this copy. It is generated when the app is built (in development, with scripts/gen-third-party).

reasons.internal: Unexpected error in the analysis engine. The details are in the logs folder (Settings → About).
reasons.invalid_params: Some value is not valid. Check it and try again.
reasons.method_not_found: The analysis engine does not know this operation: the app and the engine are different versions. Reinstall Tonalia.
reasons.track_not_found: That track is no longer in the library.
reasons.batch_not_found: That tag write can no longer be undone.
reasons.file_not_found: The file cannot be found: it may have been moved or deleted.
reasons.file_exists: A file named “{{name}}” already exists. Choose another folder or change the name template.
reasons.decode_failed: The audio of “{{name}}” cannot be read: the file is damaged or its format is not supported.
reasons.unsupported_format: This file type is not supported for this operation.
reasons.write_failed: “{{name}}” could not be written. Check that the folder has free space and permission.
reasons.verify_failed: The result could not be verified after writing it, so it was discarded. The original file has not been changed.
reasons.ffmpeg_missing: The audio component (FFmpeg) is missing. Reinstall Tonalia.
reasons.rubberband_failed: The key or tempo could not be changed (Rubber Band). Reinstall Tonalia if it keeps happening.
reasons.process_crashed: The analysis of this track stopped abruptly. Try again; if it keeps happening, the file may be damaged.
reasons.program_running: {{program}} is open. Close it and export again.
reasons.collection_not_found: {{program}}'s collection was not found. Pick its file with “Change…”.
reasons.unsupported_version: Tonalia does not recognise this version of the {{program}} collection, so it left it untouched. Check for a Tonalia update.
reasons.database_busy: {{program}} did not close properly and its database has pending changes. Open {{program}}, quit it normally and export again.
reasons.schema_too_new: This library was used by a newer version of Tonalia. Update Tonalia to open it.
reasons.model_missing: The stems model is not downloaded. Download it from Settings → Stems.
reasons.stems_missing: This track has no stems yet. Press “Separate stems” and try again.
reasons.download_failed: The download arrived incomplete or damaged. Try again: it will resume where it stopped.
reasons.network: No internet connection, or the server is not answering.
reasons.gpu_unavailable: No compatible NVIDIA GPU was found.
reasons.driver_too_old: The NVIDIA driver is too old. Update it and try again.
reasons.permission_denied: Tonalia is not allowed to access that file or folder. Check the system permissions.
reasons.not_analysed: The track is not analysed yet (it needs a key and a BPM). Analyse it first.
reasons.bpm_out_of_range: That tempo change is too large: only half to double is supported.
reasons.out_of_track: That point is past the end of the track.
reasons.pool_empty: The source has no analysed tracks. Analyse them first.
reasons.invalid_set: The set is not valid: it cannot repeat tracks.
reasons.choose_folder: Choose a destination folder or set the DAW folder in Settings.
reasons.undo_changed: Cannot undo: the file has changed since Tonalia wrote it.
reasons.undo_mismatch: Cannot undo: the backup does not belong to this file.
reasons.folder_no_tracks: Folders have no tracks of their own: choose a playlist.
reasons.folder_inside: A folder cannot be moved inside itself.
reasons.playlist_kind: That cannot be done with this kind of playlist (a folder or a smart playlist).
reasons.favorite_same: A favorite needs two different tracks.

updates.privacy: Tonalia only connects to GitHub to see whether there is a new version; it sends none of your data. Updates are signed and are never installed unless you ask.

notes.ffmpeg: Separate program Tonalia uses to decode audio.
notes.rubberband: Separate program Tonalia uses to change tempo and pitch.
notes.libsndfile: Library that comes with Rubber Band on Windows.
notes.demucsCode: Stem separation code, included in the engine.
notes.demucsModels: Stem models. They are not in the installer: they are downloaded the first time you separate stems. They are published with the Demucs code (MIT), without a separate licence.

acks.keyProfiles: Key profiles by Krumhansl and Kessler (1982), Temperley (1999) and Faraldo et al. (2016–2017), using the values published in their research.
acks.giantsteps: The key detector's weights were fitted on the annotations of the GiantSteps-MTG-Key dataset (Faraldo et al., MTG-UPF). Tonalia does not include its audio.
acks.fonts: Bricolage Grotesque, Instrument Sans and Martian Mono fonts, under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
